Traditional Pork Pie

Served at: Old Twelfth Night Wassail

Serves 8Prep 40 minCook 1 hr 15 min

Pork Pie is a classic British cold meat pie traditionally served during the Old Twelfth Night Wassail, a festive celebration marking the end of the Christmas season. This savory pie, with its rich, seasoned pork filling encased in a crisp, hot water crust pastry, is a hearty treat enjoyed by wassailers as they toast to health and good fortune for the coming year.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/2 cups (320 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 5 oz (140 g) unsalted butter, chilled and diced
  • 5 oz (140 g) lard, chilled and diced
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) cold water
  • 1 lb (450 g) pork shoulder, finely diced
  • 1/2 lb (225 g) pork belly, finely diced
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 1 tsp ground white pepper
  • 1 tsp dried sage
  • 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) cold chicken stock
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. To make the hot water crust pastry, combine flour and salt in a large bowl.
  3. In a saucepan, bring water, butter, and lard to a boil until melted, then pour the hot fat mixture into the flour mixture, stirring quickly with a wooden spoon until it forms a dough.
  4. Allow the dough to cool slightly, then knead on a floured surface until smooth.
  5. Reserve about one-third of the dough for the lid and set aside.
  6. Roll out the larger portion of dough to line a 7-inch (18 cm) deep pie tin, pressing it up the sides to form a thick crust.
  7. In a bowl, mix the diced pork shoulder and pork belly with chopped onion, white pepper, sage, nutmeg, salt, and chicken stock until well combined.
  8. Fill the pastry case with the pork mixture, pressing it down firmly to remove air pockets.
  9. Roll out the reserved dough and place it over the filling, sealing the edges by pinching and crimping the pastry together.
  10. Brush the top with beaten egg and cut a small hole in the center to allow steam to escape.
  11. Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour 15 minutes or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is cooked through.
  12. Remove from oven and allow to cool completely before slicing and serving cold, as is traditional.

Tips

  • Use a mix of pork shoulder and belly for a good balance of lean and fat, ensuring a moist filling.
  • Allow the pie to cool and rest for several hours or overnight to let the flavors develop and the filling to set.
  • Serve slices with traditional English mustard or pickles for added flavor.
